text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on SB-02: app.js:791 is verbatim '93 + Math.sin(i * 0.4) * 4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5'. I enumerated the generator: empirical min 89.000, max 99.000 over all reachable inputs, so the clamps at 792-793 (>100, <70) are provably unreachable and index.html:390-391's 'Low (50-70)' / 'Very Low (<50)' bands can never render. Means reproduced exactly: X1 93.92, X3 94.30, P1 94.29. sin period 2*pi/0.4 = 15.708 residues, confirmed. app.js:850 PAE is 0.4*|i-j| plus an offset that depends only on the row index i, so it is structurally information-free and can never show off-diagonal blocks — confirmed by reading the code. app.js:747-749 does colour spheres by letter with G/S to the High band and P/D to the Low band; the criticism that this is close to inverted for Gly is correct science. The lDDT ground truth (Mariani 2013) and the AF3 'sharply defined' quote are both accurate — I retrieved the AF3 limitations text verbatim from PMC11168924. Correction: THE ABSENCE PROOF AS WRITTEN IS FALSE AND MUST BE RESTATED. 'grep -ci pdb' over the four files returns 1 hit, at index.html:359: '...for live 3D prediction and PDB/CIF download.' The substantive claim (no coordinate or confidence file is ever read) survives — the hit is marketing prose, not code — but a claim of '0 hits for pdb' is refutable in ten seconds and would discredit the report. Restate as: 0 hits for '.pdb', '.cif', 'mmcif', 'fetch(', 'XMLHttpRequest' (I verified all five), and cite index.html:359 separately as an aggravating fact, since the UI promises a PDB/CIF download the platform cannot produce. Second correction: 'maximum attainable value on a 45x45 grid is 18.5 A' is arithmetically right but applies to exactly one entry — gridSize = min(L,45) at app.js:844, and only X1 (L=47) is truncated. For the other 24 the ceiling is lower: L=26 gives 8.4 A, L=28 gives 11.7 A, L=41 gives 16.9 A. The mismatch against the '0 - 30 A' title at index.html:397 is therefore worse than stated. Third: the four-band legend at index.html:387-392 sits inside graph-box 2 (the pLDDT chart), not the 3D box; and the chart line is a single flat cyan (app.js:804), so the legend colour-codes nothing in either panel. Finally, for the fix: AF3's confidences JSON exposes atom_plddts (per-atom) and pae; per-residue pLDDT requires the mmCIF B-factor column or an explicit per-residue aggregation of atom_plddts — the fix should say so rather than treating the two as interchangeable.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on SB-03: I fetched google-deepmind/alphafold3 docs/input.md directly and both decisive quotes are verbatim: 'If using SMILES, you cannot specify covalent bonds to other entities as these rely on specific atom names' and 'Defining covalent bonds between or within polymer entities is not currently supported', plus bondedAtomPairs 'is intended for modelling covalent ligands, and for defining multi-CCD ligands (e.g. glycans)'. I independently confirmed the AlphaFold Server allow-list: the 19 CCD codes the reviewer lists (ADP ATP AMP GTP GDP FAD NAD NAP NDP HEM HEC PLM OLA MYR CIT CLA CHL BCL BCB) plus the ten ions, with arbitrary SMILES unsupported on the public Server. None of the ten named natural products is on that list. app.js:660-671 does copy only drug.sequence; index.html:362-363 is a clipboard button plus a bare anchor to alphafoldserver.com. Zero grep hits for bondedAtomPairs, userCCD, fetch(, XMLHttpRequest. The GSK-3beta claim checks out precisely: UniProt P49841 begins MSGRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG..., residues 3-34 are exactly GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG = app.js:225 byte for byte, and Ser9 sits at peptide position 7 with no SEP modification specified anywhere (0 grep hits). AF3 emits pLDDT/PAE/pTM/ipTM/ranking score and no free energy, so the dG values cannot have come from it. Correction: One sub-claim overreaches. 'The sequences at app.js:173 and app.js:371 contain B ... and would be rejected by both the Server and the local parser.' The Server half is safe. The LOCAL parser half I could not confirm: docs/input.md says only 'a string that uses the 1-letter standard amino acid codes' and is silent on B/Z/J/X handling, and I did not read the parser source. Restate as 'rejected by the Server; local behaviour unverified — at minimum B (Asx) does not map to a defined residue.' Also, the reviewer missed a third occurrence of B: app.js:130, the CogWnt-Fzd-09 fasta in AF3_CANDIDATES, which is the string rendered in the main 3D viewer and shown in the leaderboard panel. Cite it alongside 173 and 371.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on SB-04: I extracted all 25 entries programmatically rather than trusting the citation. All four pairs are byte-identical at the cited lines with the cited metrics: app.js:153/247 (36-mer, pLDDT 94.8/94.3, dG -16.2/-17.5), app.js:173/371 (31-mer, 95.1/93.8, -16.9/-16.1), app.js:195/319 (41-mer, 93.2/92.8, -16.5/-15.7), app.js:205/361 (37-mer, 95.8/94.1, -17.2/-15.8). The determinism argument is correct, and the observation that the app's own renderer will draw pixel-identical structures and identical pLDDT curves beside contradictory summary numbers is correct because both generators are pure functions of the string. The ground-truth caveat (peptide pLDDT may legitimately differ in different complexes, but then the receptor must be an input entity with separate jobs and ipTM) is properly stated. Correction: THE FINDING IS MATERIALLY UNDERSTATED — it stops at the 25-drug array. Across all 35 sequence-bearing entries (25 drugs + 10 AF3_CANDIDATES) there are only 26 distinct sequences, and 5 of the 10 leaderboard fastas are byte-identical to 25-drug sequences with a different reported pLDDT, producing two THREE-WAY contradictions: KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG carries 94.8 (X2, app.js:153), 94.3 (B1, app.js:247) and 92.8 (CogAChE-PAS-02, app.js:131); SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC carries 93.2 (P1), 92.8 (M3) and 90.7 (CognACh-Mod-06, app.js:134). Three further cross-array pairs: app.js:163 vs :127 (97.0/96.1), app.js:215 vs :132 (93.9/93.6), app.js:225 vs :133 (92.5/91.9). So the correct statement is '9 of 35 entries are sequence duplicates and every duplicate group carries a different pLDDT', and '26 distinct sequences across 35 entries', not 'four pairs' and '21 distinct designs'. The build-time assertion in the fix must span both arrays. Separately, this finding is missing its strongest evidence — see missed_by_reviewer item 1, the thermodynamic inconsistency of every dG/Kd pair.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on SB-05: I recomputed every count from the file. Total Cys = 103; designs with >=4 Cys = 16; maximum 8, in HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (app.js:143) and PfcGluN2A-LTP-P3 (app.js:215); 11 designs with an odd count, and the reviewer's per-design list (X4:7, P2:7, P4:1, B3:5, B5:5, M1:5, M5:3, A1:5, A2:7, A3:7, A4:1) matches mine exactly. The X2 contradiction is real: app.js:152 specifies 'Cys-Lys Amide Coupling' and app.js:153 contains zero cysteine. Combinatorics verified (8 Cys -> 7!! = 105; 6 -> 15; 4 -> 3). Disulfide geometry ground truth is accurate (S-S 2.05 A, Cb-S-S ~104 deg, chi3 ~ +/-87 deg with left-handed-spiral preference) and these are exactly the quantities MolProbity/OneDep flag. Zero grep hits for disulfide, SSBOND, cystine, bondedAtomPairs. The free-thiol chemistry (scrambling, dimerisation, mixed disulfides with albumin Cys34 and glutathione) is correct, as is the point that FZD8 CRD (app.js:174) and TrkB Ig-like D5 (app.js:144) are cystine-framework-defined folds. Correction: Two counting caveats a reader will find. (1) A4 (app.js:381) appears in the odd-Cys list with C=1 only because its 'sequence' field is the prose string 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' — the C comes from 'Conjugate'. It is not a design with a free thiol. The honest figure is 10 odd-Cys designs among 24 real sequences. (2) The 11 odd-count entries collapse to 8 distinct molecules, because X4/A3 are the same 7-Cys sequence and P2/A2 are the same 7-Cys sequence (per SB-04). Neither correction weakens the finding, but both should be stated so the numbers survive checking. On the fix: gating chi3 at +/-(75-105) deg is a reasonable flag but should not be a reject — real chi3 distributions are bimodal with substantial spread, and legitimate disulfides fall outside that window. The reviewer says 'flag', which is right; keep that wording.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on SB-06: I ran the greps myself over README.md, app.js, index.html and styles.css: 0 hits for each of molprobity, ramachandran, clashscore, posebusters, rdkit, openmm, mmcif, .cif, b-factor, resolution. Confirmed that the only quality-like numbers in the platform are the synthetic curve at app.js:791 and the hardcoded strings at app.js:146/156/166/... and README.md:96-102. All four literature anchors are real and cited correctly, which I verified independently: MolProbity, Williams et al., Protein Sci 27(1):293-315, DOI 10.1002/pro.3330 (PMID 29067766); wwPDB validation, Gore et al., Structure 25(12):1916-1927, DOI 10.1016/j.str.2017.10.009 (PMID 29174494); PoseBusters, Buttenschoen/Morris/Deane, Chem Sci 15(9):3130-3139, DOI 10.1039/D3SC04185A; Engh & Huber, Acta Cryst A47:392-400, DOI 10.1107/S0108767391001071 (confirmed via Crossref). The AF3 self-reported failure modes are quoted verbatim from the paper: 'The model outputs do not always respect chirality... we still observe a chirality violation rate of 4.4% in the benchmark' and 'a tendency of the model to occasionally produce overlapping (clashing) atoms'. The argument that AF3's own documented failure modes are precisely the ones only post-hoc validation catches is sound and well-supported. Correction: No factual error. One scoping point the reviewer should make explicit, because he concedes it in the overall assessment but not in the finding: this is not an independently actionable defect today, since there are no coordinates to validate. It is a required precondition on the SB-01/SB-03 remediation, not a standing gap that can be closed on its own. As written at MAJOR alongside the others it reads as a fifth independent problem when it is a conditional sixth. Minor factual note: RDKit 2026.03.5 IS installed in the repository's own .venv — it is simply never used by the platform, which if anything sharpens the point.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on SB-07: All four defects verified directly. (1) app.js:381 is literally sequence: 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'. I ran it through the three generators: 37 characters; the pLDDT chart labels are H1, i2, s3, 14, 45, -6, P7, h8 exactly as claimed; the '14' point evaluates to 99.0 exactly; and copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) writes this string to the clipboard beneath a button offering AlphaFold Server submission. (2) I fetched the three.js r128 CatmullRomCurve3 source and the mapping is 'const p = ( l - ( this.closed ? 0 : 1 ) ) * t;' — so getPoint(i/L) returns control index i*(L-1)/L, and the displacement reaches 0.944 residues at i=L-2 for L=36 and 0.957 for L=47. Confirmed. (3) The i += 2 stride is at app.js:743 and app.js:1004. (4) SphereGeometry(2.2) at app.js:757 and SphereGeometry(2.5) labelled bindingSite at app.js:1012, both .position.set(0, 0, 0), with no relation to the bindingSites strings rendered in the same modal. The ground-truth statement (validate against the 20 standard codes, reject B/Z/J/X, key annotations to label_seq_id/auth_seq_id, define pockets from actual coordinates) is correct. Correction: Defect (3) is loosely attributed. The four-band legend at index.html:387-392 belongs to graph-box 2 (the pLDDT chart), not the 3D box, and the chart itself does plot every residue (app.js:787 loops 1..seqLen). The 'only half the residues' problem is confined to the 3D spheres, and the legend mismatch is an adjacency inference from the 3D panel's title at index.html:377, not a direct contradiction. Weaken the wording accordingly. Also, as in SB-03, the third 'B' at app.js:130 is missed. On the fix: 'reject any character outside the 20 standard codes' is too blunt for a pipeline that will later need modified residues — the validator should carry an explicit allow-list of permitted AF3 modification CCD codes alongside the 20. Finally, note that defects (2) and (3) evaporate the moment SB-01's fix lands; only (1) and (4) are independently actionable, which is why MAJOR rather than CRITICAL is the right level.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THERMODYNAMIC INCONSISTENCY OF EVERY dG/Kd PAIR — the single strongest arithmetic proof of fabrication in the repository, and the review never performs it. dG(deg) = RT ln(Kd); at 298.15 K, RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol. The 25 reported Kd values (app.js:146,156,166,...) imply dG of -11.35 to -13.77 kcal/mol, but the dG reported in the SAME string runs -15.2 to -19.5. Every one of the 25 is too negative, by 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol. Critically the offset is NOT constant (1.88 kcal/mol spread), so it cannot be rescued by a different standard state, temperature, or unit convention — if both numbers came from one calculation they would satisfy the relation exactly. The pairs are, however, almost perfectly rank-monotonic (1 inversion in 24), the signature of someone writing 'bigger dG implies smaller Kd' by hand. This is checkable by any reader in one line of Python and belongs in SB-04 as its primary evidence.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: HALF THE NATURAL-PRODUCT SMILES ARE NOT MOLECULES, AND NONE CARRIES STEREOCHEMISTRY. index.html:118 advertises 'SMILES formulation, pharmacophoric moieties, receptor binding residue coordinates, and stereochemistry' and app.js:477 renders the field as 'SMILES Formulation'. Run through RDKit 2026.03.5 (already installed in the repo's own .venv): app.js:10 Huperzine A fails to parse at the grammar level; app.js:50 Curcumin fails to parse ('OCH3' is not SMILES — it must be OC); app.js:60 Onjisaponin V is the string 'C58H92O27 (Onjisaponin V Core Skeleton)', a molecular formula not a SMILES; app.js:70 Salvianolic Acid B likewise 'C36H30O16 (Caffeic Acid Tetramer)'. Of the four that do parse, two are the wrong compound: app.js:20 Ginsenoside Rg1 parses to C38H64O14 / MW 744.9 when the real compound is C42H72O14 / MW 801.0 — and the app's own chemStruct at app.js:142 states C42H72O14, so the SMILES contradicts the formula in the same repository; app.js:30 Ginkgolide B parses to C18H22O8 / MW 366.4 when ginkgolide B is C20H24O11 / MW 424.4 (app.js:370 states C20H24O10, also wrong). And every parseable SMILES has ZERO assigned stereocentres: Rg1 has 21 unassigned, ginkgolide B 12, asiatic acid 12. A SMILES with 21 unassigned centres denotes ~2 million stereoisomers. For a platform whose warheads are dammarane and ursane triterpenoids and a cage diterpene — molecules defined by their stereochemistry — this is a first-order error, and it makes SB-06's discussion of AF3's 4.4% chirality-violation rate moot: there is no chirality in the input to violate. This deserves its own finding at BLOCKER/CRITICAL and sits squarely in the discipline (SB-06 even names RDKit as the missing tool but never runs it on the data that IS present).

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: AChE ACTIVE-SITE RESIDUE NUMBERING CONFLATES TWO DIFFERENT PROTEINS, AND THE REVIEWER CREDITS IT AS CORRECT. app.js:154 reads 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)' — Trp84/Phe330/Tyr121 are Torpedo californica AChE numbering while Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr341 are human AChE numbering (the human equivalents of the first three are Trp86/Tyr337/Tyr124). No single structure exists in which all six numbers are correct. The repo is also internally inconsistent for the same compound: app.js:12 calls the PAS tryptophan 'Trp279' (Torpedo) while README.md:32 calls it 'Trp286' (human). The overall assessment explicitly praises 'the AChE CAS (Trp84/Phe330) and PAS (Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr341) assignments' as correct and non-obvious — that credit is misplaced and should be withdrawn.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: ZERO STRUCTURAL PROVENANCE ANYWHERE IN THE PLATFORM. Not one PDB accession, UniProt accession, resolution, method, or chain/auth-numbering convention appears in README.md, app.js or index.html, yet the platform asserts residue-level binding epitopes for TrkB, AChE, Keap1, FZD8, alpha7 nAChR, GluN2A, TLR4/MD-2, Trem2, TrkA, M1 mAChR, ER-beta and EAAT2. Every residue number in the app is therefore unverifiable by construction — a reader cannot tell whether 'Keap1 Tyr334, Arg415' (app.js:164) refers to the Kelch beta-propeller of any deposited structure or to nothing. Citing the source structure and its numbering scheme is the most basic provenance requirement in structural pharmacology and the review never raises it; it should be a MAJOR finding with the fix 'every residue-level claim carries a PDB ID (or UniProt accession) and states auth vs label numbering'.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE LEADERBOARD IS RANKED BY AN UNDEFINED METRIC, AND IT IS NOT EVEN SORTED BY IT. Ranks 1-10 at app.js:125-134 are ordered by 'cei', surfaced as a table column at index.html:306 and as 'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI / 100)' at app.js:1063. CEI has no formula, units, or provenance anywhere in the code, and appears 0 times in README.md. Worse, the ranking violates its own metric: rank 3 (CogNrf-KeapDis-03) has CEI 92.1 while rank 4 (CogTrk-DeNovo-01) has CEI 93.8. SB-04 correctly says the ranking is 'ordered on invented quantities' but never notes that the ordering quantity is undefined and self-inconsistent — which is a cleaner, purely internal demonstration than any of the pLDDT arguments.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE PRIMARY 3D VIEWER IMPLEMENTS NO pLDDT COLOURING AT ALL. SB-01 and SB-02 both analyse only the modal viewer's letter-based colour rule (app.js:747-749). In update3DProteinStructure — the viewer behind the whole 'AF3 TOP 10 Candidates' tab — the residue spheres are hardcoded white at app.js:1006 (MeshPhongMaterial({ color: 0xffffff })). README.md:108 promises a 'residue-specific pLDDT color spectrum' for the '3D WebGL Molecular Engine'; in the main engine there is no colour mapping of any kind. This is a more direct README-to-code contradiction than the one the review actually cites.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO ASSESSMENT OF WHETHER THE DESIGNED SEQUENCES ARE PLAUSIBLE FOLDED ENTITIES AT ALL. Several 'binders' are highly cationic amphipathic 30-40mers — KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (app.js:153/247) and FLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (app.js:329) — which is the canonical cell-penetrating / antimicrobial amphipathic-helix motif, not an AChE gorge or LC3 binder, and is a well-known source of nonspecific membrane lysis and false-positive binding. Others are GGGGS-linked two-domain fusions (app.js:183, 235, 287, 339, 391) for which any single reported pLDDT and single Kd is meaningless because the linker is by design disordered. A structural biologist assessing designed peptides would raise both: the first as a specificity/artefact concern that invalidates the stated mechanism, the second as a reason a chain-averaged confidence number cannot be reported at all. Neither appears in the review.
